mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns during periods of rising unemployment (UNRATE increases by >0.2pp).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 4%, it indicates monetary tightening, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase and corporate earnings are pressured.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns when FEDFUNDS is above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals a strong labor market and accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns when UNRATE < 5% and FEDFUNDS > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as related sectors (e.g., construction, finance) benefit.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns during periods of increasing housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong supply-side activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as corporate productivity and earnings improve.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns during periods of increasing industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows faster than consumer prices (CPIAUCSL), it indicates strong real economic growth, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as corporate revenues and earnings improve.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns when GDPC1 growth exceeds CPIAUCSL growth.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real federal spending (RSAFS) indicates increased government demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as industries benefiting from government contracts see increased activity.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns when RSAFS growth exceeds 2%.
